questions.q: What are the three parts of an HCL block?
options: A type, optional quoted labels, and a body in curly braces
A variable, a function, and a return value
A provider, a resource, and a data source
A header, a footer, and a comment
questions.explain: Every HCL block has a block type, zero or more quoted labels, and a body wrapped in curly braces containing arguments.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid HCL list?
options: { "eastus2", "westus2" }
("eastus2", "westus2")
["eastus2", "westus2", "centralus"]
<eastus2, westus2>
questions.explain: A list in HCL is an ordered, square-bracketed sequence of values, such as ["eastus2", "westus2", "centralus"].

questions.q: How is an HCL map written?
options: An ordered sequence in square brackets
An unordered set of key = value pairs in curly braces
A single quoted string with commas
A list of numbers only
questions.explain: A map is an unordered set of key/value pairs inside curly braces, such as { project = "northbridge-retail", owner = "platform-team" }.

questions.q: Which comment style is used throughout this course and in almost every official Terraform example?
options: The hash symbol (#)
A leading semicolon (;)
Double dashes (--)
XML-style tags (<!-- -->)
questions.explain: The hash symbol (#) is HCL's preferred comment style, though two slashes (//) and slash-star block comments also work.

questions.q: What does ${ } do when used inside an HCL string?
options: It escapes special characters
It evaluates the expression inside and splices the result into the string
It marks the line as a comment
It declares a new block type
questions.explain: ${ } interpolation evaluates whatever expression is inside it — a variable reference, a function call, or arithmetic — and inserts the result into the surrounding string.
